extracted.intended_audience: inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRFs), IRF administrators and clinicians, quality reporting staff, and other stakeholders involved in IRF-PAI data collection and CMS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and implementation guidance for adopting and collecting standardized social determinants of health (SDOH) patient assessment items on the IRF-PAI for the IRF Quality Reporting Program (QRP), including item selection rationale, timing, response options, lookback periods, training, interoperability, monitoring, and data governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for SDOH domains
rubrics_metrics.description: These domains were chosen based upon literature review and expert consensus utilizing the following criteria: (1) availability of high-quality scientific evidence linking a given HRSN to adverse health outcomes and increased healthcare utilization, including hospitalizations and associated costs; (2) ability for a given HRSN to be screened and identified in the inpatient setting prior to discharge, addressed by community-based services, and potentially improve healthcare outcomes, including reduced readmissions; and (3) evidence that a given HRSN is not systematically addressed by healthcare providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domains were selected because they can be assessed across the broadest spectrum of individuals in a variety of settings; CMS' contractor reviewed >50 screening tools and convened a technical expert panel (TEP) to pare down and recommend a short list of questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and psychometric validation requirement for chosen tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The AHC HRSN Screening Tool is evidence-based and informed by practical experience; it was tested across many care delivery sites, screened more than one million Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, and was evaluated psychometrically and demonstrated evidence of both reliability and validity, including inter-rater reliability and concurrent and predictive validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relied on literature review, TEP input, and psychometric testing when selecting items; CMS disagrees that further testing is required prior to collection because of this evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect Living Situation at admission (present look-back)
rubrics_metrics.description: We proposed to require the collection of the Living Situation item at admission only. The proposed Living Situation item frames the question as, 'What is your living situation today?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The item establishes the look back period (the present) the patient should consider; collecting at admission facilitates coordinated care, continuity in care planning, and discharge planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living Situation response-option granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Living Situation response options include distinctions such as 'I have a place to live today, but I am worried about losing it in the future' and 'I do not have a steady place to live' in addition to options for unable to respond or patient declines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the additional response option indicating worry about future housing reduces ambiguity and helps identify patients at risk of losing housing due to changes (e.g., lost income) so IRFs can facilitate discharge planning and make community referrals; therefore CMS will not simplify to a simple Yes/No for this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances for patients unable or unwilling to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: For patient interview assessment items, proposed response options include codes for 'Patient declines to respond' and 'Patient unable to respond'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRFs are expected to use these options when appropriate; CMS notes IRFs have experience administering interview items to impaired patients and will provide coding guidance and training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for collection (admission-level collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed new assessment items (Living Situation, Food, Utilities, modified Transportation) are collected at admission only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission collection is 'as close to the time of admission as possible' to inform immediate care and discharge planning; CMS will develop coding guidance using public feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food assessment uses two items with three-point frequency scale and 12-month look back
rubrics_metrics.description: Two proposed Food assessment items use responses: (0) Often true; (1) Sometimes true; (2) Never True; plus (7) Patient declines to respond; and (8) Patient unable to respond. The items use a 12-month look back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past testing found higher sensitivity when using both items (affirmative response to either yields sensitivity of 97 percent) versus a single item; CMS chose three-point scale because AHC HRSN Tool was tested and validated using it and because IRF-PAI already contains items with varying scales; CMS defends 12-month look back due to dynamic nature of HRSNs and published evidence of fluctuation over quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities assessment item scope and 12-month look back
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Utilities assessment item captures threats or problems across electric, gas, oil, or water services and uses a 12-month look back period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considers capturing all utility types important to understand needs related to equipment (e.g., oxygen, ventilators, LVADs) and to inform discharge planning; CMS defends 12-month look back based on evidence of HRSN fluctuation and IRF capability to collect from complex patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation item modification: 12-month look back and simplified response
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposed to modify the Transportation item to: (1) use a defined 12-month look back period (instead of six to 12 months); and (2) simplify the response options to align with the AHC HRSN Screening Tool (two response options: Yes; No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to reduce ambiguity and improve validity; current IRF item separates medical vs non-medical barriers—proposal aligns IRF item with Hospital IQR and IPFQR wording to promote standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability and standardization across programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Using common standards and definitions for new assessment items is important to promote interoperable exchange of longitudinal information between IRFs and other providers to facilitate coordinated care, continuity in care planning, and discharge planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial alignment with Hospital IQR and IPFQR (same SDOH domains) will facilitate longitudinal collection; CMS has proposed similar items in SNF QRP, LTCH QRP, and Home Health QRP to further standardize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and implementation resources to reduce burden
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will provide training resources in advance of the initial collection to ensure IRFs have the tools necessary to administer new items and reduce burden of creating their own resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources may include online learning modules, tip sheets, Q&A documents, recorded webinars and videos; CMS anticipates making materials available (target mid-2025) so IRFs have several months before required collection and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRFs may collect additional SDOH beyond required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals would not preclude IRFs from choosing to screen their patients for additional SDOH they believe are relevant to their patient population and community (e.g., disability-status, caregiver availability, independent living status, ability to return to work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS encourages IRFs to collect any additional information they believe relevant to inform care and discharge planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collected SDOH data and rulemaking constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: We proposed the four new SDOH assessment items to permit development of statistical tools to maximize value of Medicare data. Any updates to the IRF QRP measure set or payment system would be addressed through future notice-and-comment rulemaking, as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes recent use of Health Equity Confidential Feedback Reports and states that developing measures or payment impacts based on SDOH data will follow formal rulemaking processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing monitoring and potential administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all new assessment items, CMS will monitor all aspects of data collection and submission under the IRF QRP, and should we identify changes in provider behavior, we will take the appropriate administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine item and measure monitoring will assess implementation; CMS will also use monitoring to refine coding guidance as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for look back period choices (12 months vs shorter periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS defends 12-month look back periods for Food and Utilities items because an individual's HRSNs can fluctuate over time; studies show substantial quarter-to-quarter fluctuation, so a longer look back captures needs IRFs should consider for care and discharge planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will consider public feedback in developing coding guidance but maintains that longer lookback windows comprehensively capture changing needs; shorter (3-month) windows were proposed by some commenters but rejected by CMS for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and operational feasibility assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS believes collection of these new SDOH items is within the normal day-to-day operations of IRFs and that IRFs are likely already collecting some of this data due to existing discharge planning requirements (see regulation §482.43(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites that IRF admission criteria and existing items (e.g., discharge living setting) do not substitute for admission-level SDOH items; collecting at admission provides actionable information earlier in care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical support for retaining multiple items when sensitivity differs
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing showed that collecting both Food assessment items yields higher sensitivity (97%) for identifying respondents with food needs compared to a single item (93% or 82% depending on item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses such empirical sensitivity evidence to justify including multiple items despite commenter suggestions to combine them to reduce burden.
